resources.string: Watches only which app comes to the foreground, so the bottom screen can be turned off for the apps you choose. It never reads screen content.
Turn the bottom screen back on when you leave
If this is off the bottom screen stays off after you leave a selected app, until you turn it back on with the dual-screen button. Unticking an app always brings it back either way.
If you press the dual-screen button and pick a mode yourself, this app stops touching the setting until you leave that app.
Also sets the focus-lock settings the built-in menu sets, so windows and hardware keys stay on the top screen. Restored when the bottom screen comes back.
Deep off: actually power the panel down

The built-in menu only covers the bottom screen with a black window, so the panel stays lit. This powers it off for real. The dual-screen button still works: pressing it powers the panel back so you can see the menu. A screen off/on also brings it back.
Stops SystemUI popping up its rotate icon in the corner. This one is device-wide, not per app, and applies the moment you flip it. Turning it back off restores whatever the setting was before.
